clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man with recurrent group A Streptococcal (GAS) cellulitis and impetigo, with poor antibiotic compliance, presented with throbbing pain in the legs and arms, and a diffuse desquamative rash involving the face, torso, and upper and lower extremities with a morbilliform pattern and tender vesicular varicella-appearing lesions on the right upper back. Sparing of palms, soles, rectum, oral labia, and mucosa was noted. Admission vitals showed tachycardia (HR 130), hypertension (158/116 mmHg), and tachypnea (RR 22). Initial laboratory studies revealed azotemia (BUN 24 mg/dL) and leukocytosis (17.9 thou/mm³), indicating systemic inflammatory response. Blood cultures were positive for Staphylococcus aureus. A skin biopsy of the dorsum of the right hand showed psoriasiform hyperplasia with atypical T cell infiltrate and eosinophils. T cell gene rearrangement studies did not reveal clonal cells, ruling out cutaneous lymphoma. Initial treatment with IV vancomycin for 4 days did not improve the rash or pruritus. Antibiotics were changed to IV cefazolin due to concern for drug reaction, and the patient was started on prednisone 60 mg PO and topical Triamcinolone 0.1% cream applied copiously and faithfully BID. Desquamation and erythema resolved by day 12 with persistent topical corticosteroid application. The patient followed up with Dermatology at least 3 times within the first 2 months post-discharge with continued topical corticosteroid therapy.
